rules.title: Relocation payments for no-fault evictions (owner/relative move-in, demolition/removal, temporary capital improvement, substantial rehabilitation)
rules.requirement: If you get an eviction notice for owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal of the unit, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation, the landlord must pay you relocation money. For notices served 3/1/26 to 2/28/27, that is $8,245 per tenant, up to $24,733 per unit, plus $5,497 more for each tenant who is 60 or older or disabled, or for a household with minor children.
rules.key_value: $8,245 per tenant; max $24,733 per unit; +$5,497 per elderly (60+)/disabled tenant or household with minor children (notices served 3/01/26–2/28/27)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants in San Francisco units covered by the Rent Ordinance's eviction controls who get an eviction notice for owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal from housing use, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation. The amount depends on the date the eviction notice is served and changes every March 1.
rules.exemptions: Relocation for temporary capital improvement evictions of less than 20 days is governed by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9, not Rent Ordinance § 37.9C.
rules.quoted_span: Relocation Payments for Evictions based on Owner/Relative Move-in OR Demolition/Permanent Removal of Unit from Housing Use OR Temporary Capital Improvement Work* OR Substantial Rehabilitation

rules.title: Relocation payments for Ellis Act evictions
rules.requirement: If you are evicted under the Ellis Act (the owner is taking the units off the rental market), the landlord must pay relocation money. For notices served 3/1/26 to 2/28/27, that is $11,110.05 per tenant, up to $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 more for each tenant who is 62 or older or disabled.
rules.key_value: $11,110.05 per tenant; max $33,330.13 per unit; +$7,443.90 per elderly (62+)/disabled tenant (notices served 3/01/26–2/28/27)
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants in San Francisco who get an Ellis Act eviction notice. The amount depends on the date the notice is served and changes every March 1.
rules.citation: S.F. Rent Ordinance (S.F. Admin. Code ch. 37), Ellis Act relocation provision; section not cited in document
rules.quoted_span: Relocation payments for tenants evicted under the Ellis Act

rules.title: Relocation for temporary capital improvement displacement under 20 days (San Francisco)
rules.requirement: If you have to move out for less than 20 days for capital improvement work in San Francisco, your relocation payment is set by California Civil Code § 1947.9, not by the city's Rent Ordinance § 37.9C.
rules.coverage_conditions: Temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days in San Francisco.
rules.quoted_span: The amount of relocation payments for temporary capital improvement evictions for less than 20 days is governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 and not by Rent Ordinance Section 37.9C.
rules.conflict_note: The state statute, not local Rent Ordinance § 37.9C, sets relocation for temporary capital improvement evictions of less than 20 days. The document does not give the state amounts.

notes:
I pulled 3 rules from this Rent Board page, all in the just_cause_eviction category (relocation payments):

1. **San Francisco no-fault eviction relocation (§ 37.9C).** Used the current 3/01/26–2/28/27 amounts. The status is in force.
2. **San Francisco Ellis Act relocation.** Used the 2026–27 amounts. The page does not give a section number, so the citation field says only that it is the Rent Ordinance's Ellis Act provision. That is why confidence is lower.
3. **Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9.** Comes from the footnote saying state law, not § 37.9C, sets relocation for temporary capital improvement evictions under 20 days. The page gives no amounts or effective date, so confidence is low. Tagged as preemption because a state statute governs that subset instead of the local ordinance.

**Archive rows not recorded separately:** amounts back to 2006 for evictions served in earlier periods. They are the same rules at older rates, with a new rate each March 1.

**Rent cap and deposit interest:** the page links to current rent increase and deposit interest rates, but gives no figures, so nothing was extracted for those categories.

**Age thresholds differ:** the extra payment starts at age 60 for no-fault evictions, also covering households with minor children, and at age 62 for Ellis Act evictions.
